messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test expects that when using CSVFormat with a specified header (using withHeader), the CSVPrinter should print the header line automatically before the records when printing records.

From the bug report and the test, we see that CSVFormat.withHeader(String...) creates a new CSVFormat with the header set. However, the CSVPrinter constructor simply stores the format but does not do anything to automatically print the header line. It currently lacks logic for printing the header line.

Looking at the CSVPrinter constructor code snippet:
- It only checks the constructor params and stores the format. There is a TODO comment mentioning header printing but no implementation indicating that header is printed at construction or on first record print.

The printRecord methods just print the records themselves without checking or printing any header row.

The bug report also confirms that withHeader in CSVFormat is only used by CSVParser currently, and CSVPrinter does not support printing the header line automatically.

Hence the root cause of the test failure is that while the CSVFormat supports the concept of a header, the CSVPrinter does not use this header information to print the header line automatically. Therefore, the test expects a header line printed but the printer outputs only user-called record lines.

This explains why the test fails as the output does not start with the header line. The feature for CSVPrinter to honor CSVFormat headers and print header lines is missing.

No recent bug reports are directly related to printing headers or CSVPrinter's handling of headers. They focus more on input parsing or format validation, which is unrelated to the printing header issue.

Summary: The bug occurs because CSVPrinter does not implement any mechanism to print the header line from the CSVFormat header, so when constructed with a format with a header, it still does not emit the header line before printing records.

Next step would be to add or investigate if there is any method in CSVPrinter meant to print the header line, or to extend CSVPrinter to check for a header and print it the first time printRecord is called. The CSVPrinter constructor or printRecord method are likely places to implement this.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
